15.reason: The 'as ... as' frame is the marker WAEC students are taught to read as simile, so D is what many setters would intend, especially since this is the only line in the extract with that frame. But 'as cool as you please' compares the speaker to nothing; 'as you please' is an idiomatic intensifier meaning 'as coolly as could be wished', so a student who knows that a simile compares two unlike things has good grounds to reject D. A, exaggeration, is the natural fallback, since the line overstates the speaker's poise in the boastful spirit of 'Phenomenal Woman', though it is not strong hyperbole either. Neither option clearly beats the other on the merits, and a well-prepared student could not tell whether the setter was testing the surface 'as' pattern or the effect of the idiom.
